notes: sm_120 (RTX 50xx / RTX PRO Blackwell): the Dockerfile adds 12.0 to torch_cuda_arch_list from v0.9.2 (PR #19794, milestone v0.9.2); v0.9.0 and v0.9.0.1 fail with 'no kernel image is available'.
sm_121 (GB10 / DGX Spark) is listed with the sm_120 minimum by CUDA binary compatibility within the same major architecture: not verified on hardware.
Kernel coverage on sm_120 kept improving after v0.9.2 (FP8/NVFP4 MoE, FlashInfer): prefer the recommended tag; very old tags may run a model but miss fast kernels.
Default image CUDA: 12.8 up to v0.11.x, 12.9 from v0.12.0, 13.0 from v0.20.0 (needs driver >= 580). '-cu129' variants of newer tags exist for CUDA 12.9 drivers.
The image entrypoint is 'python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server' up to v0.11.x and 'vllm serve' from v0.12.0: newer tags take the model as a positional argument (--model is deprecated there).
sm_70 (V100) left the default arch list in v0.20.0; maxTagBySm is the last tag known to include it.
recommendedTag is the newest stable release on Docker Hub when this file was updated; it is still to be verified on the RTX 5090 in the real-hardware run.
server-cuda is built with CUDA 12.8.1 (covers sm_120); server-cuda13 uses CUDA 13. Entrypoint is /app/llama-server, default port 8080.
Some users report server-cuda13 falling back to CPU where server-cuda works: server-cuda stays the default.
ghcr.io gives no anonymous size API: the download size is shown as unknown.
Release tags on Docker Hub: vX.Y.Z (CUDA build of the release), vX.Y.Z-cu130 (CUDA 13.0), '-runtime' variants without the build tools (about 1.4 GB smaller). rocm/xpu/cann tags are for other GPUs.
The image has no server entrypoint: the command is 'python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path … --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000'.
On Windows SGLang runs only in Docker Desktop with the WSL2 GPU; native only on Linux.
v0.5.21 was the newest stable release (2026-10-01, about 15.2 GB) when this file was updated; not yet run on the RTX 5090 here.
